blocks.h2: Getting Your Sump Pump Ready for Storm Season
blocks.body: Before spring, pour a bucket of water into the pit and watch the pump start and stop. Check that the discharge line outside isn't blocked or frozen. If the pump is more than 7 years old, consider replacing it before it fails. And add a battery backup if you don't have one. In a storm like May 2020, power outages and heavy rain can arrive together.

blocks.h2: Sump Pump Questions From Skokie Homeowners

items.q: Can you install a sump pump in a basement that doesn't have one?
items.answer: Often. We cut a pit where water collects, install the pump and run a discharge line outside.

items.q: Do I need a battery backup?
items.preview: If you store anything or use the basement, yes.
items.answer: If your basement is finished or holds anything you care about, yes.

items.q: How long do sump pumps last?
items.answer: Most last about 7 to 10 years, less if they run often.

items.q: Can my sump pump drain into the floor drain?
items.answer: No. That sends groundwater into the sewer, which adds to backups. It should discharge outside.

items.q: Can a sump pump drain into the sewer?
items.answer: Usually not. Sump water should go outside, away from the house.

items.q: How much does sump pump installation cost in Skokie?
items.preview: It depends on the pit, pump and backup. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on whether a new pit is needed, the pump and whether you add a backup. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
